assumptions.label: Typical easement (right-of-way) width, 115 kV line (Georgia Transmission)
assumptions.section: Typical Transmission Line Easement Widths (approximates) - Roadside | Cross Country
assumptions.exactExcerpt: 115 kV Line Single pole 25-42.5 feet + 100 feet
assumptions.note: Georgia Transmission Corp. fact sheet (2017). The two values are the Roadside and Cross Country columns. Typical is the cross-country width, printed as '+ 100 feet'; I read that as 100 ft or more, so 100 is the conservative end. Low is the bottom of the roadside easement range (25-42.5 ft), used where a line runs beside a road right-of-way. The H-frame row also says '+ 100 feet' cross-country. The sheet gives no upper bound. As a cross-check, MISO's indicative width is 90 ft (rowWidthFt.115.miso). I found no public DESC or Georgia Power statement of a 115 kV width.

assumptions.label: Typical right-of-way width, 230 kV line (DESC / SCE&G certificate application)

assumptions.exactExcerpt: WIDTH OF RIGHT-OF-WAY: 100 FEET (Typical) DESIGN VOLTAGE: 230 kV
assumptions.note: South Carolina Electric & Gas (now Dominion Energy South Carolina) filed this Siting Act application on July 7, 2010 (cover letter, page 2). It covers an 8.0-mile 230 kV line between two substations in northeast Columbia, Richland County (page 5), and states a typical width of 100 ft. The excerpt supports only this single value, so no low or high is given. Georgia Transmission gives 100 ft (single pole) to 125 ft (H-frame) cross-country (rowWidthFt.230.gtc). MISO's indicative width is 125 ft (rowWidthFt.230.miso).

assumptions.label: Right-of-way easements priced at full USDA-based land value (MISO planning convention)
assumptions.unit: fraction of land value per acre
assumptions.section: 2.1 Common Cost Categories - Right-of-Way, Land Acquisition, and Regulatory and Permitting (printed page 6)
assumptions.exactExcerpt: MISO has three categories of land costs: pasture, crop, and urban/suburban. MISO utilizes the annual USDA Land Values summary to estimate the value of pastureland.
assumptions.note: This is a planning convention, not an observed ratio of easement price to fee value. MISO says its right-of-way costs cover land easements and prices them from the USDA land value per acre (pasture; cropland = 3x pasture; urban/suburban = 5x pasture). The same page says 'All land costs are based upon the acreage of land that the new transmission line would traverse' (also verified). The guide applies no easement discount factor, so the implied share is 1.0. That share is my inference; MISO does not state it. MISO adds a separate acquisition cost per acre on top (rowAcquisitionCostPerAcre). No SC or GA source states a typical share.

assumptions.label: Example easement payment as a share of land value (Grain Belt Express, Missouri 2016)
assumptions.unit: fraction of average fee value per acre
assumptions.section: Compensation Calculation - Easement Payment
assumptions.exactExcerpt: Clean Line will pay 110% of the average value of the land, based on recent sales in the county
assumptions.note: This is one developer's landowner offer, filed with the Missouri PSC as Schedule DKL-3 (June 2016), for a line with an easement 'approximately 150-200 feet wide' (page 1). It is not SC or GA and not a typical utility share. The source contradicts itself: page 2 repeats the 110% rule, but its worked example prices the easement at 100% of the stated $5,000/acre market value ('9.1 acres x $5,000 (price per acre offer) = $45,500', verified on page 2). Treat it only as evidence that easement payments can reach or exceed fee value, and use it only as a high sensitivity case.

assumptions.label: New single-circuit 115 kV line, exploratory cost per mile (MISO; Mississippi as Southeast proxy)
assumptions.unit: USD/mile (MTEP24 $: guide says data are in 2023 $, escalated 5% to 2024; incl. 30% contingency + 7.5% AFUDC)
assumptions.section: 4.1 Table 4.1-1: Exploratory cost estimate - AC transmission, new single circuit transmission line $/mile (printed page 38)
assumptions.note: The columns are 69 / 115 / 138 / 161 / 230 / 345 / 500 / 765 kV (header verified on the same page). The second value in each row is 115 kV: typical is Mississippi, $2.2M; low is Montana, $1.8M (the table minimum, shared with North and South Dakota); high is Louisiana and Mississippi, $2.2M (the table maximum, shared with Texas). SC and GA are not MISO states; using Mississippi as the closest Southeast proxy is my choice, not the source's. The footnote reads 'Includes contingency (30%) and AFUDC (7.5%)'. MISO says these $/mile figures are built from the guide's own assumptions and cost data (page 39), and that it assumes new right-of-way for all new lines (page 7), so this per-mile cost already includes right-of-way land and acquisition. Do not add an avoided right-of-way land value on top of it. MISO also says it 'does not recommend using exploratory cost estimates for any solution idea in the regular planning cycle' (page 39).

assumptions.section: Purpose Statement
assumptions.exactExcerpt: Cost data was escalated from 2025 U.S. dollars to 2026 U.S. dollars at a rate of 4% for most cost categories
assumptions.note: Optional. The rate applies 'for most cost categories'; the same sentence says MISO separately benchmarked certain costs with suppliers and vendors, so it is not a uniform rate. It can move the MTEP24 per-mile values to 2026 dollars at the user's choice, but applying 4% over more than one year is my extrapolation: the source states only the 2025-to-2026 step, and MTEP24's own dollar year is ambiguous (page 2 says 2023 $, escalated 5% to 2024). The MTEP26 guide (June 10, 2026) keeps its tables in the 'Exploratory Cost Estimate Workbook for MTEP26', an xlsx the excerpt checker cannot verify, so I did not quote 2026 $/mile values.

assumptions.label: Crew mobilizations avoided when two lines on shared right-of-way and structures are built together (SCE&G testimony, summarized in a joint proposed order)
assumptions.section: Joint Proposed Order (unnumbered 'ORDER NO. 2011-'), SC PSC Docket 2011-325-E, filed Dec. 14, 2011 - proposed-order page 10, summarizing SCE&G testimony (Tr. II, p. 93)
assumptions.exactExcerpt: building them at the same time will avoid the need to mobilize construction crews twice to work on the same structures and thereby will reduce construction costs
assumptions.note: This is qualitative. The passage is in a Joint Proposed Order that SCE&G, the Town and the County filed for the Commission's consideration (cover letter, page 3: 'Joint Proposed Order for the Commission's consideration'). It is not an issued Commission order; the order number is blank (page 43). It summarizes testimony by SCE&G witness Mr. Young (page 51). The statement concerns two SCE&G lines, the St. George Segment and the Lake Murray Line, which 'will share the same right-of-way and the same structures'. Building both at once avoids mobilizing crews twice, so one mobilization is avoided. No dollar amount or percentage is given. It applies only when projects share work sites or structures, and no source establishes that for any DESC-Georgia Power pair. The UI must say so.

assumptions.label: Georgia ITS new transmission line miles requiring new right-of-way, 2025-2034

assumptions.exactExcerpt: New Transmission Lines Requiring New Right of Way Voltage (kV) Lines Miles Lines Miles 500 5 163 12 543 230 26 211 37 530 115 7 49 10 69 Total 38 423 59 1142
assumptions.note: Context for scale only, not an input to the per-pair calculation. The two column pairs are First 5 Years and Total 10 Years. Over 10 years there are 543 miles at 500 kV, 530 at 230 kV and 69 at 115 kV, 1,142 miles in all. The first-5-year total (423 miles) was removed from 'low' because it is a subset, not a lower estimate of the 10-year figure. The same table lists 982 miles to be rebuilt or reconductored on existing right-of-way over 10 years. The ITS is owned by four participants, so these miles are not Georgia Power's alone (page 6, verified: facilities 'individually owned and maintained by Georgia Power Company (GPC), Georgia Transmission Corporation (GTC), MEAG Power (MEAG) and Dalton Utilities (DU)'). The source is the public-disclosure version of the IRP appendix.

issuesFixed: avoidedMobilizations was mislabelled as an SC PSC order. The cited passage (PDF p52) is in a Joint Proposed Order that SCE&G, the Town and the County filed on Dec 14, 2011 'for the Commission's consideration' (cover letter p3); its order number is blank ('ORDER NO. 2011-', p43). I corrected the label, section, note and the source's title, publisher and publishedAt (2011-12-14). The value (1 avoided mobilization) is unchanged and still supported as SCE&G witness testimony (Mr. Young, p51; Tr. II p.93).

MISO MTEP24 dollar year: the unit said '2024 $', but page 2 says 'All cost estimate data in this document are in 2023 U.S. dollars' and then 'escalated ... to 2024 U.S. dollars at a rate of 5%' (verified). I changed the unit to 'MTEP24 $' with that wording on lineCostPerMile.115/.230/.500, .115.rebuild, .230.rebuild, rowAcquisitionCostPerAcre and rowPermittingCostPerAcre.

lineCostPerMile.115/.230/.500: the low and high came from state rows (Montana, Louisiana) outside the quoted Mississippi row. I replaced exactExcerpt with the contiguous Louisiana-to-Montana rows of Table 4.1-1, verified FOUND on page 39, which contain the typical, low and high for all three voltages. All values were re-checked against the full 15-state table and are correct.

Double-counting risk: MISO's new-line $/mile figures are 'based on the assumptions and cost data shown in this guide' (p39, verified), and MISO assumes new right-of-way for every project except rebuilds (p7, verified). So they already include right-of-way land and acquisition. I added a warning to the lineCostPerMile and rowAcquisitionCostPerAcre notes, and MISO's own caution against using exploratory estimates in the regular planning cycle (p39, verified).

landValuePerAcre.SC (low 4100) and landValuePerAcre.GA (low 4670, high 5100): I removed the low and high because they come from the cropland (p11) and pasture (p15) tables, not the page-9 excerpt. Those values stay available as separate keys with their own verified excerpts. All USDA numbers were re-read and are correct (GA farm real estate 4,950, SC 4,900; cropland GA 4,670, SC 4,100; pasture GA 5,100, SC 4,500).

context.gaItsNewRowMiles10yr: I removed low=423. It is the first-5-year total, a subset rather than a lower estimate of the 10-year total. I also added that ITS mileage covers GPC, GTC, MEAG and Dalton Utilities, not Georgia Power alone (p6, verified).

easementShare.cleanLineMO: the source contradicts itself. The page 2 worked example prices the easement at 100% of the stated $5,000/acre market value ('9.1 acres x $5,000 (price per acre offer) = $45,500', verified), while the text says 110%. I added this to the note and removed the claim that it is a 'merchant HVDC' line, which the cached document does not state.

easementShare.misoConvention: I replaced the excerpt with a contiguous passage (p7, verified) stating that right-of-way costs 'cover land easements' and are priced from USDA pasture value, which supports the convention directly. The note now says plainly that the 1.0 share is an inference, because MISO states no discount factor.

costEscalationPerYear: I added that the 4% applies only 'for most cost categories' and that MISO benchmarked certain costs separately, so it is not a uniform rate. I also relabelled it as the 2025-to-2026 step.

lineCostPerMile.230.descNewExample: I fixed a garbled page reference ('page 49's counterpart') to page 12, removed an unsourced 'near Savannah' location claim, and quoted the substation scope ('will require a new CIP Hut'). I also checked that the total equals the previous-years amount plus 2026.

I found no public source stating DESC's 115 kV or 500 kV right-of-way widths. Those widths come from Georgia Transmission, with MISO as a cross-check.

I found no published cost-per-mile guide for the Southeast (SC, GA or SERTP). The per-mile values here are MISO-footprint values (Mississippi as proxy), plus DESC-derived ratios (project total / stated miles) that are single-project planning estimates, one of which includes substation scope.

The MISO MTEP26 guide keeps its $/mile and right-of-way tables in an xlsx workbook that the excerpt checker cannot verify, so the MTEP24 PDF tables are quoted. The MTEP24 dollar year is ambiguous: page 2 says both '2023 U.S. dollars' and escalated to 2024.

USDA NASS excerpts are column-ordered runs of numbers because pdftotext reads each table one column at a time. Each note gives the row order and year. The UI should show the section title and page so a judge can see which row each value comes from.
Page numbers for the MISO guides are PDF page indexes. Printed page numbers are one lower and appear in each section field.
